data.method: files routed by the pipeline's detectLanguageFromPath, ordered by a hash of their relative path and capped deterministically; each lane parsed in its own child process with a fresh module; ERROR nodes and MISSING tokens counted separately; the rate compared against a pinned per-lane floor whose sample digest must match

layers: corpus routing (the pipeline's own detectLanguageFromPath, including the .h sniff)
pinned grammar per lane (wasm), one fresh module per lane in its own child process

limitations.description: This measures the GRAMMAR's surface, not recovery quality: symbols flow through an ERROR region, so a high rate and a zero rate can both be 'no symbol loss' — that is why F5 stays green and why this gate exists separately.
The corpora are local checkouts; each lane records its repo pin so a moved corpus is visible beside its floor.
A lane whose candidate set changed reports sample-moved and is NOT compared — the honest state, not a pass. The gate exits 2 in that case.

The rate is the full production-routed surface, so the c figure includes plain C headers and the cpp figure includes the headers production sniffs as C++. The per-extension split is recorded beside every row so these reconcile with the .c-only census in reviews/m49-w17-parse-success-census.md.
